core_conclusion: At the declared m*=1, gamma*=4 protocol, the sampled amplitude-period map contains pinned and transporting integer winding states, and representative transporting states satisfy relative-periodic closure and cross-solver Floquet attraction.

design_system.theory_data_semantics: Evidence-bearing numerical panels use executed simulation outputs. Color and marker/line semantics are redundant where series are compared. Illustrative schematic elements are explicitly non-evidentiary.
design_system.scale_policy: Shared scales for direct comparisons; transformed/log scales only when explicitly labeled and scientifically necessary.
design_system.legend_policy: Compact legends or direct labels placed in data-sparse regions.

provenance.notes: All quantitative evidence panels derive from verified executed simulations. Explicit schematic panels are illustrative only and are not used as numerical evidence.

caption: Figure 6. Two-dimensional vector mode locking under the declared deterministic protocol. (a,b) Integer windings m and n over the 91 sampled rocking-amplitude/period points at theta=1.5 deg, m*=1, and gamma*=4; the map contains pinned (0,0) as well as transporting integer-winding states. (c) The tau*=40 slice shows the sampled vector staircase. (d) Independent DOP853 and Radau monodromy calculations agree on the extremely small leading Floquet spectral radius and relative-periodic closure of the representative (1,-1) orbit. The map is sampled and protocol specific; it is not a continuous phase diagram or a proof of global uniqueness.
